newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/8.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/8.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.0/8.5 percent on Thursday morning on sustained ample supply.
Dealers said liquidity remained ample, but tom/next swaps were volatile on anticipation of Friday liquidity.
The central bank supplied 230 billion rupiah on Thursday.
Tom/next swap was last at 1.00/1.05 after touching a high of 1.7 points in the morning. Overnight swap was at 0.25/0.35.
One local bank dealer said tax payments were usually not large in the first and third week. But they would probably rise next month due to fiscal ending.
Another dealer said preparation for possible tighter market prompted operators to cover short swap positions which helped drive swap rates higher across the board.
He said operators were also seen factoring in the new reserve requirement rate effective from April 16.
Ample supply kept longer-term rates lower, with one-month money offered at 12.0 percent and three at 13.5 percent.

The central bank lowered its three-month bilateral SBIs by 25 basis points but all other rates were stable. It offered four-to-six day SBIs at seven percent, seven-to-eight day at eight percent, 11-13 day at 9.5 percent, 14-15 day at 10.0 percent, one-month at 11.0 and three at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 8.21 percent, compared with 8.98 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said the market remained quiet. One said some focus was on the zero-coupon bonds of Semen Gresik.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was last at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
